newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein's Adams cancels British parliament visit.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein's Adams cancels British parliament visit.

text.p: Irish Republican leader Gerry Adams has cancelled a controversial private visit on Thursday to Britain's parliament, an opposition legislator who invited him said.
The visit by the leader of Sinn Fein, the Irish Republican Army's (IRA) political wing, would have come just three days after British police foiled what they said was an imminent IRA bomb attack.
Police shot dead an IRA suspect in London on Monday and seized 10 tonnes of explosives in raids that dealt a severe blow to IRA guerrillas who are battling to oust Britain from Northern Ireland.

Opposition Labour Party member of parliament Jeremy Corbyn, who was roundly criticised by his own party for issuing the invitation to Adams, said the Sinn Fein leader had cancelled his visit to the House of Commons (lower house) but gave no reason, the Press Association news agency reported.

The agency quoted a spokesman for Corbyn as saying it was Adams who had pulled out and that that the invitation had not been withdrawn in the face of threats from the Labour leadership to throw Corbyn out of the party.

Adams had hoped to launch his autobiography in the House of Commons building on Thursday, but the launch was cancelled by parliamentary officials over the weekend so Corbyn issued his private invitation instead.

Adams was elected MP for West Belfast in the 1980s but never took his seat in the House of Commons. He said he regarded Britain as an occupying power in the province and has refused to take an oath of allegiance to the British monarch.
He has visited parliament several times in the past few years since as a former legislator he cannot be barred.
